fixes.explanation: Paul says, “But you, O man of God, flee from these things…” (1 Timothy 6:11). Just before this, he warned about the love of money (1 Timothy 6:10), so these are the things Timothy is told to run from. FLEE, friend. Nobody flees at a stroll.

That would be a nice, calm evening class, but it's not what Paul wrote. He says to flee from these things, right after warning about the love of money (1 Timothy 6:10). Nobody takes notes while running for the door. Class is dismissed, friend, and so is the notebook.

Profit sounds tempting, but Paul says flee. Right before this, he warned that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil (1 Timothy 6:10). So these things aren't a business opportunity for Timothy. The word is flee, friend, not cash in.

Right. Paul says Timothy made the good confession “…before many witnesses.” (1 Timothy 6:12). Many, friend, so it wasn't private with no one else around. The text doesn't say where it happened, but it does say people were there. I bet that's a moment you'd remember.

Paul says Christ Jesus “…made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate…” Pilate was the governor Jesus was handed over to (Matthew 27:2). So Paul points Timothy to Jesus' own example. Timothy confessed before many witnesses, and Jesus made His confession before Pilate.

Felix was a governor (Acts 23:24), so I see where your head went. But Paul names someone else here. In verse 13 it's Pontius Pilate, the governor Jesus was handed over to (Matthew 27:2). Two governors, one name in the verse, friend.

Paul says it plainly: “No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him.” He says it right after saying that the Sovereign One dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). So True is the answer. Unapproachable light, friend, and I'll let Paul's words stand.

Paul actually says it: “No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him.” That comes right after he says the Sovereign One dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). So True was the answer. Unapproachable light, friend, and no one has ever seen Him.
Paul finishes with, “To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen.” After saying who the Sovereign One is, he ends with praise. I think that's a fitting way to close after a description like that.
Saving has its place, but it's not the word Paul uses here. He says to be generous and ready to share. Ready to save would be a different instruction, friend. Paul's word is share.

Favor is lovely, friend, but it's not in Paul's sentence. He says the generous are “…treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future…” So the answer is the foundation, not the neighbors' good opinion. That foundation is what Paul's whole sentence stands on.

Paul says to avoid “…irreverent, empty chatter…” and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge.” That's a lot of talk with nothing inside it. It's like a cookie box that's all ribbon and no cookies.
Paul says the opposite. Of this so-called “knowledge,” he says, “…which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith.” (1 Timothy 6:21). Some did, friend, so that statement doesn't hold.
Paul closes with, “Grace be with you all.” After all that fighting, guarding and fleeing, the blessing he leaves them with is grace. I like how that lands. It's like the last batch coming out warm.
Peace is a lovely blessing, but it's not the word Paul uses here. His closing blessing in this letter is “Grace be with you all.” So the answer is grace, friend.

Timothy could use some strength after that list, and I'd bet he'd say so too. But Paul doesn't end with it. His closing blessing is “Grace be with you all.” Grace is the blessing he names for them all.
